items.finding: eval_harness/win32.py create_job() returns a job handle that no code path closes. terminate_job() calls TerminateJobObject but never CloseHandle, and ProcessTree never releases self._job, so a long-running harness process leaks one kernel job handle per run_bounded call (bounded by attempts x gates, so tens per round).
items.verification: CONFIRMED against the code. There is no CloseHandle on the job handle anywhere and ProcessTree holds _job for the object lifetime.
items.decision: Deferred, not fixed. Pat proposed calling a new close_job() from a reap-adjacent cleanup once the tree is done. That is refuted by a committed test: test_a_grandchild_of_a_parent_that_exits_at_once_is_still_reachable_to_the_reap calls tree.survivors() AFTER runner.reap(), so on Windows a closed handle would make job_process_ids raise. It also contradicts the deliberate hold documented on ProcessTree (JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE means a released handle kills the tree early). A correct fix needs an explicit handle-lifecycle contract on ProcessTree, which this task neither specifies nor tests. Belongs with the attempt.py task that owns attempt teardown, or a follow-up PRD.
